facts.fact: The World Bank's diagnostic, prepared in 2015 from consultations in May-June 2014 and March 2015, states that the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare operates the civil register recording births and deaths, with a central registrar at its Monrovia office.
facts.system: Civil register of the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare

facts.fact: The diagnostic states that the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare maintains an electronic database of births, though not in real time, holding 415,596 records (287,939 from county registrars and 127,657 from the central registrar, MOHSW 2014), and that deaths and marriages are not properly registered and remain to be captured electronically.
facts.system: Civil register of the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare

facts.fact: The diagnostic states that a birth notification form is filled in triplicate at birth, two copies go to the district registrar, who records the birth, transmits the information to the electronic database at the Ministry in Monrovia and issues the certificate; the database is not kept in real time, and the report does not say whether the registrar's own record is digital or how the transmission is made.
facts.system: Civil register of the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare

facts.fact: The diagnostic states that since 2011 the government has established 14 birth registration centres, as registrars, in different counties, beside the central registrar in Monrovia, and that their records reach the Ministry's electronic database (287,939 records from county registrars, MOHSW 2014); it gives no total of local offices and does not say the centres themselves make the digital entry.
facts.system: Civil register of the Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
